name: Tracheobronchopathia Osteochondroplastica

criteria.description: Presence of multiple submucosal nodules composed of bone and cartilage in the trachea and main bronchi
Evidence of airway narrowing or obstruction on bronchoscopy or imaging
No evidence of malignant or infectious etiology causing nodular lesions
Histopathological confirmation showing submucosal ossification and cartilaginous nodules

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple characteristic submucosal nodules in the trachea/bronchi with airway obstruction and exclusion of malignancy or infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Bronchoscopic visualization combined with histopathology is the gold standard for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Submucosal bony and cartilaginous nodules in trachea and bronchi
Airway obstruction due to nodular lesions

rare.symptomName: Respiratory failure due to severe airway obstruction

imaging: CT scan showing irregular nodular calcifications along the anterior and lateral walls of the trachea and main bronchi
Bronchoscopic visualization of multiple submucosal nodules sparing the posterior membranous wall
other: Histopathology revealing submucosal ossification and cartilaginous nodules without malignant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid deposits visible on biopsy with Congo red staining
Diffuse airway involvement including posterior membranous wall
Inflammatory cartilage destruction affecting ears, nose, and airways
Systemic symptoms such as fever and arthralgia
Airway involvement includes inflammation and collapse rather than nodular ossification

redFlags: Progressive airway obstruction causing respiratory distress
Hemoptysis indicating possible airway mucosal ulceration
Rapid worsening of symptoms suggesting alternative diagnosis such as malignancy
references: Lieberman J. Tracheopathia osteoplastica. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1964;73:1121-1130.
Seijo LM, et al. Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica: clinical and pathologic study of 41 cases. Medicine (Baltimore). 2001;80(5):378-390.
Marchand E, et al. Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica: a rare cause of chronic cough and airway obstruction. Eur Respir Rev. 2019;28(151):190012.
